NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Families want to share their best tools in one basket: share them with rules, or keep tools in each family.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has noticed that every family has one good adze, one good knife, one good digging stick, and uses them twice a month. (subject.He/she) wants one big shared tool basket, with rules for borrowing. (friend) says nobody will clean anything and the tools will vanish. What should the village do?

text_only.reason: the word's everyday sense (a thing, a sound or a person out of sight for a moment); nobody leaves the village -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The shared basket is set up, with a keeper and rules: return it clean, return it by dark. In the first month, three tools vanish and one is returned covered in fish. After that, people get the hang of it. Everyone has better tools than before.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: Families keep their own tools. Nothing vanishes. Families with good tools do well; families without borrow quietly from friends. (subject) starts lending (subject.his/her) own to anyone who asks.
